asks: What does Silo change in the traffic it reads?
answer: Silo changes the traffic it reads in three ways only, and records each change with what it replaced. It puts a secret to use: it swaps the secret's value into the place the secret names, or signs the request again with it. It keeps a secret out: it puts a placeholder in a reply in place of a secret's value or of a token made from it, and, once you make a value found in a conversation into a secret, it puts that secret's placeholder in place of the value in every later model request. And on your yes, or by a rule you set, it sends a request changed so that its effect can be undone. The record never holds a secret's real value. A reply that waits while a precaution answers about a tool call in it is passed on unchanged, or not at all. A request that a rule or a budget refuses is not changed: it is not sent, and the agent program gets an error.
